summary: Listed as a Georgia lookout tower at the Twiggs County community of Tarversville; no source found on its history or the site today.

evidence.quote: Tarversville is an unincorporated community in Twiggs County

evidence.supports: named for Hartwell Hill Tarver, owner of a nearby plantation
evidence.quote: The community was named after Hartwell Hill Tarver, owner of a large nearby plantation.

evidence.supports: post office 1826 as Tarver's Store, renamed 1831, closed 1880
evidence.quote: A post office called Tarver's Store was established in 1826, the name was changed to Tarversville in 1831, and the post office closed in 1880.
A historical marker was erected at the site in 1960.

notes_for_editor: Thin, and the tower itself is unconfirmed beyond the list line. A search surfaced a 103.6 m (339.9 ft) antenna structure registered at Tarversville (towerdex.com, tower 1242420), which appears commercial. That page returns HTTP 403 to the cache reader, so it is neither footnoted nor described in the story; whether it stands on the lookout site is unknown and should be checked before any 'today' wording is written. Search hits on Fort Twiggs (1813 blockhouses) and the 1901 courthouse fire are unrelated to a lookout and are excluded. The story runs about 92 words, below the guide's ~120-word floor; hold or publish as a stub.
